title: Sell Mineral Rights in Bobtown, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Bobtown, PA | Greene County
metaDescription: Bobtown, PA mineral owners in Greene County: get a clear cash offer on your Marcellus royalty interest, no obligation to accept.
heroLead: Bobtown sits in Greene County, the most heavily drilled county in Pennsylvania's Marcellus play, so your royalty check has real production history behind it.
intro: If you own minerals near Bobtown, you're in the middle of the densest Marcellus and Utica development anywhere in Pennsylvania. Greene County has more producing unconventional wells than any other county in the state, and operators like CNX Resources and EQT have held and developed leasehold here for well over a decade. That means your royalty check, whatever it looks like today, is tied to some of the most active, best-understood production in the entire play.
We've sold our own family's minerals before, and even in a county this active, we found the paperwork wasn't always explained clearly. That's what we fix before we ever talk numbers.

sections.heading: The most drilled county in the state
paragraphs: Greene County's combination of thick Marcellus shale and deep Utica and Point Pleasant potential has made it a priority target for operators since the early days of the play. Bobtown-area tracts are very likely part of an active, established spacing unit, with a real, traceable multi-year production history rather than a speculative or early-stage one.
This is wet-gas territory, meaning natural gas liquids make up a meaningful share of production and a corresponding processing deduction shows up on your royalty statement.

sections.heading: Why so many owners here still feel shortchanged
paragraphs: Even with heavy production, the post-production deduction issue affects Greene County owners just as much as anywhere else in the state. Pennsylvania's Kilmer v. Elexco ruling lets operators net gathering, compression, and processing costs against your royalty, and in a wet-gas county like this one, that deduction line can be substantial. It's one of the most common reasons Greene County owners we talk to decide it's time to sell rather than keep watching a shrinking check they can't control.

Add in the Guaranteed Minimum Royalty Act, which sets a legal floor of one-eighth on the gross value before deductions, and you have a system that guarantees you something but leaves a lot of room for the net number to disappoint.

sections.heading: Confirming your interest in an active unit
paragraphs: We trace title through the Greene County Recorder of Deeds, confirm your decimal interest against the specific unit your tract participates in, and review your recent statements to build an offer based on real numbers.

faqs.question: Why is Greene County drilled so much more heavily than other PA counties?
faqs.answer: It sits over some of the thickest, most productive Marcellus shale in the state, plus significant deeper Utica and Point Pleasant potential, making it a priority for major operators.

faqs.question: What's the Guaranteed Minimum Royalty Act actually guarantee me?
faqs.answer: It sets a legal floor of one-eighth of gross value as your royalty rate under Pennsylvania law, though post-production deductions can still be taken from that share under current case law.

faqs.question: Is a well in a heavily drilled county worth more to sell?
faqs.answer: Often, since there's more production history to base a value on. We'll review your specific unit's data before quoting a number.
